title: Batch-state preemption corruption causing intermittent token duplication and p95 latency spikes
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: During a regional capacity reclaim event (preemption cycle) the serving runtime's batching state occasionally became inconsistent between the scheduler and worker kernels. This manifested as duplicated tokens in responses for a subset of requests and transient p95/p99 latency spikes on affected hosts. The behavior appears when preemption interrupts an in-flight batch while KV-cache warmup and kernel handoff are occurring. Impact: Intermittent user-facing incorrect token output and latency regressions for ~0.8% of requests on impacted nodes over a 6-hour window. Scope: Hosted API customers in region us-west-2 on runtime-1.22 serving certain GPT-style models with mixed-precision kernels and autoscaling enabled.

investigation_notes: Log correlation showed preemption SIG messages from the cloud provider present within 200ms of the first duplicated token in the response stream.
Heap/stack traces indicate worker kernel continued to append tokens to an in-memory batch buffer after scheduler marked the batch as 'requeued', causing stale pointers to be flushed twice.
KV-cache warmup concurrently touched shard metadata leading to non-idempotent write of 'last_emitted_token' for a subset of requests.
Repro harness triggers the failure reliably when preemption is simulated with 50-70% batch fill levels and mixed-precision quant kernels enabled.
Telemetry: 0.8% of requests across affected hosts experienced duplication; p95 latency increased by ~180ms during the window.
mitigations: Immediate: Reroute traffic away from affected host pools and disable aggressive preemption autoscale policy for the short term.
Hotfix (deployed 2026-02-09): On preemption, workers perform an atomic batch checkpoint and yield without flushing in-flight batch buffers; KV-cache warmup is paused until handoff completes.
Medium-term: Add canary gating to preemption policy and increase minimum drain timeout for runtime-1.22 clusters.
Long-term: Redesign batch lifecycle to use immutable batch snapshots for kernel handoffs and make KV-cache warmup idempotent under retry.
